messages:
maria: quick sync — proposing a 'traffic aperture' controller for canaries + a 'rollback leash' to collapse reach fast. idea: central controller expands aperture in discrete ticks, local routers enforce aperture tokens. if a failure signal arrives, leash collapses aperture to 0 for affected path. low blast and fast recovery in one model.

devon: sounds interesting. who owns aperture state? central service, or per-cluster leader?

maria: central coordinator stores target aperture per route (percent) and a monotonic epoch. local routers request tokens and track local acceptance window. controller pushes epochs via streaming config.

sam: question: how do we detect the affected path quickly enough to trigger leash? we can't rely only on error-rate spikes from the central metrics pipeline — too slow.

maria: agree. hybrid signal: local probes + short-window aggregated alarms. local router can preempt and request immediate leash collapse from controller if it sees consecutive probe failures on >x% of replicas. controller still validates then broadcasts.

anya: runtime concern: collapsing aperture instantly will hurt KV cache hit ratios for user sessions. we need to gracefully degrade so we don't double-cache-miss thundering herd.

luis: maybe introduce a short 'drift window' where aperture collapse also signals cache-affinity TTL extension on golden path to avoid parallel cold starts. basically tell runtimes: keep recent cache entries 5s longer while aperture moves.

maria: exactly — leash collapse has two phases: collapse-routing (immediate) and cache-grace (soft, configurable TTL).

devon: how does this play with autoscaler? if we collapse aperture, we might leave GPUs idle or trigger scale-to-zero. autoscaler must be told not to destroy warm nodes immediately.

anya: autoscaler hint API sounds necessary. controller should post preserve_hint for N seconds when leash triggers. autoscaler consumes hints and delays eviction.

sam: observability: we need both token-level metrics (tokens issued, tokens used), aperture percent timeline, leash events, and per-shard preempt signals. suggest a small schema:

```
controller.aperture_percent: 0..100
controller.epoch: int
router.tokens_issued: int
router.tokens_used: int
leash.event:{shard, cause, time, actor}
```

maria: good. also want an end-to-end SLI: time-to-collapse (ms), time-to-recover, and post-collapse error delta.

devon: policy expressiveness: operators want rules like "expand 5% every 2m until p95 latency > 300ms or error > 0.5%". do we bake this DSL into controller or allow external policy service to drive aperture values?

luis: simplest: controller has a builtin conservative policy and accepts external overrides via policy webhook. that lets SREs run experiments without code changes.

maria: +1. controller evaluates local signals and can accept webhook advises. must rate-limit external overrides.

sam: playbook: on leash trigger, send slack alert + open incident lightly, auto-rollback option depends on policy tag (experimental vs stable). We should default to collapse aperture but not auto-roll underlying model version unless explicit.

anya: runtime API sketch for routers:

```
GET /aperture/<route> -> {epoch, percent, token_quota}
POST /aperture/claim -> {token_id, shard}
POST /leash/collapse -> {epoch, reason}
```

devon: simpler for v1: streaming SDS-style connection that pushes epoch/percent and soft commands. reduce chattiness.

maria: agreed. streaming for scale, fallback HTTP for emergency triggers.

luis: testing: we need a simulator that replays request streams and simulates aperture ticks + leash commands so we can tune expand/collapse rates and cache-grace windows.

maria: i'll open an RFC draft with the config knobs, metrics, and playbooks. one more: security — leash commands must be signed and scoped per-team. we don't want noisy teammates collapsing global traffic.

devon: authn/authz + audit logs. controller should record who initiated leash (automated rule, webhook id, or person).

sam: +1. Also add a circuit-blacklist to keep known-bad paths from reopening automatically for a cooldown period.

anya: runtime note: make token issuance idempotent so retries don't leak capacity. token format should be epoch+nonce+sig.

maria: thanks all. next steps: i'll draft RFC and include a sample policy DSL, streaming proto sketch, and the simulator plan. can we reconvene Friday?

devon: Friday works.

luis: I'll mock an autoscaler hint API prototype beforehand.

sam: I'll draft the observability schema and a couple alert rules.

deploy-bot: deploy:traffic-aperture-controller v0.1 -> staging succeeded :rocket:
